messages:
alex: Quick follow-up from the attention-kernel RFC — we need a concrete ops playbook for when Triton kernels regress on long sequences.

jessica: Agreed. Main concerns: 1) perf cliff on >8k tokens, 2) maintainability of Triton custom ops across cuda versions, 3) fallbacks that don't blow latency SLOs.

sam: From runtime side: we can short-circuit to CUTLASS kernels for blocks that fail autotune, but that requires extra compilation artifacts and ~10-20% memory overhead for dual-kernel support.

priya: Ops question — how do we signal a global fallback? Do we want a per-model rollout flag or region-level routing?

ben: Data from last week: Triton wins p50/p95 up to 4k, beyond that CUTLASS slightly better for causal-attn in fp16 on A100. Link to bench: https://internal/bench/1865 (see table).

jessica: Sounds like hybrid strategy: prefer Triton for common seq lengths, CUTLASS for long-tail. Need explicit policy: sequence threshold + dynamic fallback.

alex: Action item proposal: (A1) define kernel selection policy config, (A2) implement runtime switch with metrics gating, (A3) add CI matrix for CUDA versions. Who owns what?

sam: I can take A2. Plan: add a pluggable KernelSelector interface, with implementations: triton, cutlass, ref-emulation. Selector decision inputs: model_id, seq_len, device_caps, historical_latency. Example pseudo-config: 
```
kernel_policy: 
  - seq_len <= 4096: prefer: triton
  - seq_len > 4096: prefer: cutlass
  - degrade_on_error: fallback_to: ref-emulation
```

priya: I'll own A3 (CI) — need to know which CUDA+Triton combos to validate. Please send the matrix.

ben: I'll own A1 (policy defaults) + benchmarks for corner cases. Will draft a suggested policy and dataset (mix of short chat, long context docs, and code).

jessica: Two more considerations: KV-cache layout differences (Triton kernels assume packed KV memory) and quantization paths (int8 kernels behave differently). We must ensure seamless cache migration on fallback.

sam: Good point. Implementation note: runtime should maintain unified KV view and insert adapter shims on kernel swap. That avoids model version churn.

alex: Risk register for the playbook: 
- Operational: increased binary footprint (+10-20%).
- Reliability: more moving parts => more places for regressions.
- Cost: CUTLASS may use slightly more GPU time at p50 for short seqs if chosen incorrectly.
All need mitigations.

priya: Ops mitigation: feature-flag rollout per dedicated cluster, gradual ramp + circuit-breaker if error rate > 0.5% or latency > SLO.

ben: Bench mitigation: add synthetic worst-case tests (8k+ with long kv reuse) in nightly runs. Tag regressions into JIRA.

jessica: Security/compliance note: private deployments may not allow dynamic download of kernels. For Redwood Private, we must provide pinned artifacts and an offline fallback.

alex: Final set of immediate action items (owners & due dates):
- A1 policy draft (ben) due in 3 business days.
- A2 KernelSelector PR (sam) with unit tests and feature-flag gating in 7 business days.
- A3 CI matrix + pinned CUDA combos (priya) in 5 business days.
- KV-cache adapter spec (jessica + sam) in 4 business days.
- Nightly bench integration (ben) in 10 business days.

sam: Noted. I'll start branch kernel-selector/v1 and add basic metrics emission: kernel.chosen, kernel.fallback, seq_len_bucket.

deploy-bot: deploy status: stub infra for feature flags exists in staging. Use flag: rollout.kernel_selector.staging.

priya: I'll reserve a dedicated cluster for canary (region us-west-2-dedicated1) — please add me to PR for infra changes.

alex: Thanks everyone. Let's reconvene in 7 days with PRs and bench results. :thumbsup:

jessica: Added a follow-up doc skeleton: https://internal/docs/kernel-selection-playbook (will populate A1/A4).

ben: I'll post initial bench numbers in that doc today.

sam: If anyone hits a blocker with Triton API changes, ping me in-thread.

alex: Closing thread — keeping this as the canonical ops plan for Triton/CUTLASS adoption.
